verdict.rationale: Letta documents its own memory-maintenance mechanisms. Dreaming uses background subagents to consolidate lessons and update memory, /doctor audits the memory hierarchy for duplication, and /remember lets the agent decide where a lesson belongs and commit the update to MemFS. None of these sources explicitly describe detecting contradictions or superseding stale facts, so the core story is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of contradiction detection and supersede/merge semantics, examples of conflicting facts being resolved, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the memory layer to update, supersede, or merge memories when new information contradicts what was stored

citations.quote: Dreaming uses background subagents to review recent conversations, consolidate useful lessons, and update memory without interrupting your active work.
If the memory hierarchy has drifted or grown too large, run /doctor to audit placement, duplication, and system-prompt token usage.
The agent decides where the lesson belongs and commits the update to MemFS.
